Permute treatment in space across every donor

Source: R/scm_placebo_permutation.R
scm_placebo_permutation.Rd

Refits fit_scm() once per unit, each time pretending that unit is the treated one and that the rest of the pool are its donors. The result is the reference distribution rmspe_pvalue() ranks against, and the set of grey placebo paths behind an Abadie-style gap figure.

Usage

scm_placebo_permutation(Y, N0, T0, X = NULL, ...)

Arguments

Y

Outcome matrix, units x periods, controls first and the treated unit last.

N0

Number of control units.

T0

Number of pre-treatment periods.

X

Optional units x predictors matrix, rows aligned with Y.

...

Passed to fit_scm() – outcome_periods, bias_correct, v_method, bc_donors and friends. The same arguments are used for the treated fit and every placebo, which is the point.

Value

A list with results, a tibble of one row per unit (unit, treated, att, pre_rmspe, post_rmspe, rmspe_ratio and their _raw counterparts computed before bias correction), gaps, a units x periods matrix of the corrected gap paths, and gaps_raw, the same before correction.

Details

The treated unit is always excluded from the donor pool of a placebo fit. If it were left in, a placebo could reproduce itself out of the genuinely treated unit's post-treatment trajectory, which would import the effect being tested into the null distribution.

Everything is deterministic: the simplex solve is Frank-Wolfe from a fixed start and the bias correction is a regression, so no seed is involved and repeated calls agree exactly. That is the difference between this and the placebo variance in fit_sdid(), which is simulated.

See also

rmspe_pvalue() for the ranking that turns this into a p-value, and fit_scm() for the fit it repeats.

Examples

set.seed(1)
Y <- matrix(rnorm(6 * 8), nrow = 6,
            dimnames = list(c(paste0("d", 1:5), "treated"), 2010:2017))
Y[6, 7:8] <- Y[6, 7:8] + 3
scm_placebo_permutation(Y, N0 = 5, T0 = 6)$results
